thread.title: Bill Miller: Apple shares look 'reasonably attractive' amid stock's plunge

author: Holden Wilen
title: Bill Miller: Apple shares look 'reasonably attractive' amid stock's plunge
text: – Reporter, Baltimore Business Journal Jan 3, 2019, 12:00pm EST With Apple Inc. shares falling almost 10 percent, famed investor Bill Miller says he thinks the stock is "reasonably attractive." Apple shares are plunging Thursday after the tech giant lowered its revenue guidance for the first quarter, blaming a slowdown in China's economy and people waiting longer to upgrade their iPhones. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) shares were down to $144.39 in mid-day trading, dragging the rest of the stock market. Miller, founder and chief investment officer of Baltimore-based Miller Value Partners, has spoken glowingly about Apple on numerous occasions over the last few years and called the iPhone "a completely revolutionary product." While Miller's funds no longer have a stake in Apple, Miller said in an email to the Baltimore Business Journal he continues to own shares of the company personally. His funds pulled out of Apple during the second quarter, according to federal filings. Miller, who beat the S&P 500 for 15 straight years as a fund manager at Legg Mason Inc., said he thinks Apple is still a good stock to own. "I think there are still better values out there but at today’s price it looks reasonably attractive for those looking for a high quality company with a fortress balance sheet, decent dividend that will grow, and a valuation that is well below the market’s price earnings ratio," Miller told the BBJ. Baltimore-based T. Rowe Price Group Inc., which has $1.03 trillion in assets under management as of Nov. 30, has also been a major investor in Apple. The stock is a top holding in many of T. Rowe Price's (NASDAQ: TROW) mutual funds that have beaten the S&P 500 over the last couple of years. T. Rowe Price funds hold roughly 29.5 million shares as of Sept. 30, according to a November filing. The stake is currently worth about $4.25 billion, down 36 percent from $6.63 billion at the end of September. Another Baltimore mutual company, Brown Advisory, owns 157,660 shares. The firm's stake is worth $22.7 million.
